content: Penicillin G benzathine, marketed as Bicillin L-A, should be used exclusively for the treatment or prevention of infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria. This approach is essential to minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the efficacy of Bicillin L-A and other antibacterial agents. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform the empirical choice of treatment. Intramuscular administration of penicillin G benzathine is indicated for the treatment of infections caused by penicillin-G-sensitive microorganisms that are susceptible to the low but prolonged serum levels characteristic of this specific dosage form. The therapeutic approach should be based on bacteriological studies, including sensitivity testing, as well as the patient’s clinical response. The following infections typically respond to appropriate doses of intramuscular penicillin G benzathine: 1. Mild-to-moderate infections of the upper respiratory tract caused by susceptible strains of streptococci. 2. Venereal infections, including syphilis, yaws, bejel, and pinta. Penicillin G benzathine is also indicated for prophylactic use in certain medical conditions: 1. Rheumatic fever and/or chorea: Prophylaxis with penicillin G benzathine has been demonstrated to be effective in preventing recurrences of these conditions. 2. It has also been employed as follow-up prophylactic therapy for rheumatic heart disease and acute glomerulonephritis.
